entries.title: Raw Storage initial state, explicit IDs and empty batches
entries.evidence: Fresh original MemoryStorage capture has no conversation 1; an empty batch commits at seq1; explicit unminted conversation99 commits and raises next mint to100. Original MemoryStorage starts nextId=2 and original SQLite metadata starts next_id='2', next_seq=1, so ID 1 is reserved but never materialised: harness.root() stages tx.createRootConversation() with ownerless ownership inside its own commit, and every original test or benchmark that addresses conversation 1 creates it with an explicit conversation write (testing/storage-conformance.ts:32, testing/storage-benchmark.ts:93). Upstream has no implicit-root read path and no persisted config version at all; its only versioning is the SQLite schema migration table (version 1 initial schema, version 2 sleeping status). Native previously preinstalled root1 in initialState, required it in restoreCheckpoint and therefore fabricated a record the original Storage never held.
entries.fix: Separate raw Storage initialisation from Session root bootstrap. Implement original raw empty-batch sequence semantics and atomic allocator advancement for explicit IDs, with global type collision checks. Preserve native transaction ID reservation and writer ownership rather than deleting them.
acceptance: Replay storage-boundaries.json through the public native SQLite boundary with no preparatory minting: fresh root absent, empty batch accepted at seq1, explicit99 accepted, next mint100; original outbox replay and reopen. Concurrent allocator/explicit-ID, collisions, backend rollback and uncertain outcomes must preserve uniqueness.
entries.blocker: Native config version 2 is a native-only persisted-format marker: upstream persists no config version, only the SQLite schema migration table. Version 1 files keep their implicit reserved root, so their fresh-state shape stays different from a version 2 store, and data written while the root was fabricated cannot be rewritten as if its owner had committed it. Session/Harness root bootstrap consumes one sequence on a fresh store, so sequence-sensitive fixtures must acquire the root explicitly the way the original tests do. Broader raw Storage duplicate/update policy remains under D12 review.
verification: TestV150StorageFreshRootAbsent: fresh raw store has no conversation, HighWater 1, first mint 2, explicit root creation accepted, duplicate claim refused, root survives reopen.

TestSQLiteRootConfigVersionCompatibility and TestSQLiteUnknownConfigVersionIsCorrupt: version 2 fresh store rejects a conversation-scoped write until the owner creates the root; version 1 store keeps its implicit root, refuses a duplicate claim and keeps its data across reopen; version 3 config is ErrCorrupt.
TestHarnessRootBootstrapsReservedConversation: root absent before use, Harness.Root stores it as a committed write, reserved identity never minted, persisted across reopen.

TestPiDurableV150PublicStorageCommitReplaysCapturedOriginalBatches: unchanged captured batches replay at their original sequences against a version 1 store; TestPiDurableV150PublicStorageCommitEnforcesIDOwnership replays the original root create-then-duplicate-conrefuse pair.
Full durable suite: 0 failures in 360.203s with GOMAXPROCS=2 -p 1; go vet, pinned staticcheck, logging gate and parity-register checker pass.
entries.resolution: Raw Storage no longer fabricates the reserved root. initialState() holds no records and reserves allocator position 1, so the first mint is 2; restoreCheckpoint no longer requires conversation 1. Harness.Root/RootWithInit materialize conversation 1 through tx.CreateConversation inside their own commit (the native equivalent of tx.createRootConversation), and a second claim of the identity is refused. New native SQLite files write config version 2 and carry no root; config version 1 files, which were written while the root was fabricated and never persisted a root write, keep their implicit reserved root so their existing data retains the semantics its writer intended, and unknown config versions are ErrCorrupt rather than being guessed at. Version 1 compatibility is a native-only shim: upstream persists no config version. Empty batches and explicit raw IDs keep their earlier resolutions. The native test corpus now declares its root dependency: fixtures that address conversation 1 create it before the store is owned (seedRootConversation, the apply helper, and the sqliteStore/sqliteStoreFresh split), and seq-relative replay fixtures run against a version 1 store so every captured sequence number and document point stays intact.
